title: The Full Workflow
description: Real-world tasks combining everything you've learned.

levels.title: Plan before you type
levels.lesson:
Real shell work rarely involves a single command. A typical task looks like this:

1. Navigate to the right place — `cd`
2. Check what's there — `ls`, `find`
3. Create the structure you need — `mkdir`, `touch`
4. Read or inspect files — `cat`, `grep`
5. Reorganise — `cp`, `mv`, `rm`

The skill isn't memorising flags — it's knowing *which* command belongs at each step. This unit strings it all together with realistic tasks.
levels.example:
$ cd /home/user/projects
$ ls
myapp
$ mkdir -p myapp/src myapp/tests

challenge.instruction: Navigate to `/home/user/projects`, then create two directories inside `myapp`: `src` and `tests`.

levels.title: Setting up a project
levels.lesson:
A common first step for any project is creating a predictable directory structure and a few starting files:

```
myapp/
  src/
    main.sh
  tests/
    test-main.sh
  README.md
```

You already know all the commands for this. The only new skill is doing them in the right order — you can't `touch` a file inside a directory that doesn't exist yet.
levels.example:
$ mkdir -p myapp/src myapp/tests
$ touch myapp/README.md myapp/src/main.sh

challenge.instruction: Inside `/home/user/projects/myapp`, create: `README.md` at the top level, `src/main.sh`, and `tests/test-main.sh`.

levels.title: Cleaning up and archiving
levels.lesson:
Projects accumulate clutter — duplicate files, empty directories, temporary files. A tidy structure is easier to navigate and easier to grep.

A typical cleanup sequence:

```
find . -name '*.tmp'       # find the clutter
rm <whatever-find-found>   # remove it
cp -r project project-v1   # archive the current state
```

challenge.instruction: Archive your work: copy the entire `projects` directory to `projects-v1` in your home directory, then verify the copy exists.

levels.title: FINAL CHECKPOINT
levels.lesson:
This is the full course checkpoint. You'll use every command taught across all six units:

`pwd` `ls` `ls -a` `cd` `mkdir` `touch` `cat` `rm` `rm -r` `echo` `whoami` `cp` `mv` `find` `grep`

There's no one right sequence. Explore, inspect, and build.

challenge.instruction: Complete this multi-step task: (1) Navigate to `/home/user`. (2) Create a directory called `capstone`. (3) Inside `capstone`, create a file called `summary.txt`. (4) Copy `notes.txt` into `capstone/notes-copy.txt`. (5) Find all `.txt` files under `/home/user`.
